lessonTitle: 8. One and zero at work. The idea of number in the ancient world
lessonTitleEnglish: One and zero at work. The idea of number in the ancient world
source: Based on the topics of the Armenian grade 5 mathematics textbooks

stages.headline: Thanks to zero, ten digits can write any number. Without zero we could not tell 205 from 25.
stages.headlineEnglish: Thanks to zero, ten digits can write any number. Without zero we could not tell 205 from 25.

stages.headline: Place units are 1 followed by zeros; when multiplying them, the zeros add up.
stages.headlineEnglish: Place units are 1 followed by zeros; when multiplying them, the zeros add up.

stages.headline: People have long thought about number. Pythagoras said 'All is number'. The sign for zero was invented in India.
stages.headlineEnglish: People have long thought about number. Pythagoras said 'All is number'. The sign for zero was invented in India.

stages.headline: How many zeros does one million have?
stages.headlineEnglish: How many zeros does one million have?

stages.headline: How many zeros does 10 · 100 · 1 000 end with?
stages.headlineEnglish: How many zeros does 10 · 100 · 1 000 end with?
stages.problemText: How many zeros does 10 · 100 · 1 000 end with?

stages.headline: Two zeros were appended to the right of 37. How many times larger did it become?
stages.headlineEnglish: Two zeros were appended to the right of 37. How many times larger did it become?
stages.problemText: Two zeros were appended to the right of 37. How many times larger did it become?
stages.solutionSteps: 1. We get 3 700. 2. 3 700 = 37 · 100, so it became 100 times larger.
stages.solutionStepsEnglish: 1. We get 3 700. 2. 3 700 = 37 · 100, so it became 100 times larger.
